transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (VP Eng, Atlas Commerce), Priya Sharma (Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Infra), Aisha Khan (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Renewal coming up EOY, Atlas interested in adding EU region capacity and moving some workload to Dedicated pools. Discussed contract extension options and benchmarks to validate latency and throughput in EU. Action items: pricing, SOC2 and deployment docs, EU benchmark schedule.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, appreciate it. so this is just a quick renewal and expansion check-in, want to make sure we're aligned on capacity, regions, and any open security or contract questions before you hit renewals later this year. jordan, do you want to kick off with where things stand on your side?
[00:12] Jordan Lee: yeah, sure. thanks maya. overall things are go, we see a steady 35% q/q growth in usage, esp around checkout heuristics and search rerank. our main asks are twofold: one, we need predictable dedicated capacity for holiday season traffic spikes; two, we need an EU region for data residency and to cut latency for EU customers. also procurement is asking about contract extension options, we might want 12 to 18 month term.
[00:34] Maya Chen: perfect. that's super helpful. owens — sorry owen — can you speak to the Dedicated options and how we handle multi-region?
[00:41] Owen Patel: yep, absolutely. so with Redwood Dedicated you can reserve GPU pools per region, we typically recommend sizing by peak rps and p95 latency targets. we have autoscaling and burst capacity options for holiday bursts. for EU specifically we can spin up a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 or similar — note there is a lead time for reserved capacity setup if you want committed SLA. one thing to call out, we also support routing rules so traffic from eu can be pinned to eu instances to preserve data residency.
[01:06] Priya Sharma: quick question on quantization and model variants — we've been running a mix of q4 and q8-lite models. will Dedicated support the same optimized kernels? we can't afford regression on generation quality.
[01:17] Owen Patel: absolutely, Dedicated runs the same serving runtime — same KV cache behavior, same compilation and kernel selection. i will say sometimes the perf profile varies by hardware generation; we'll provide a quantization/profile recommendation for your workload. we can also pin a model version for the rollout, and if you want we can run a short A/B traffic split to verify quality under the new config.
[01:36] Carlos Mendes: on the networking side, we'll need VPC peering and private IP connectivity. also curious about KMS integration — we use an HSM-backed key manager, want to ensure encryption-at-rest keys are customer-managed.
[01:49] Samir Rao: yes, Samir here — we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments and Dedicated can be configured to use your keys. we'll send the KMS integration guide and HSM notes after this call. for VPC peering, we have a private control plane option and we can coordinate with infra to set up the network ranges and firewall rules.
[02:03] Aisha Khan: procurement question — if we extend to 18 months and add EU region, is there a discount band for committed spend? also SLA credits?
[02:11] Maya Chen: we typically offer stepped discounts for longer commitments, and we can include a multi-region add-on discount in the renewal proposal. SLA credits are available for Dedicated contracts depending on the tier; we'll include the SLA table and examples in the proposal. i'll include pricing tiers for 12 vs 18 month terms.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: good. another technical check — our latency SLO for EU must be p95 < 120ms for the embedding pipeline. will Dedicated in eu meet that?
[02:34] Owen Patel: that's a reasonable target. we'll run a targeted benchmark with your model and sequence lengths. to set expectations: p95s depend on model size, batch sizes, and prefix caching; if you're using prefix caching and smaller batches, we often see sub-100ms p95 on eu region for the models you mentioned. i'll scope out the test plan and we can run it next week.
[02:52] Priya Sharma: we also want the ability to failover to us-east if eu capacity is constrained. does Redwood provide transparent fallback between regions?
[03:00] Owen Patel: yes, smart routing can be configured with failover policies. you can set a primary region and a fallback region; we can also configure cost-based routing or latency-based. note that failing over across regions could have data residency implications, so we'll make sure that's part of the policy and documented.
[03:14] Jordan Lee: on the contract side, what about data retention — we need log audit window to be 12 months and full traceability for tokens requested by security audits.
[03:24] Samir Rao: we can support longer retention for audit logs as an add-on, and we provide request-level tracing and token-level cost breakdowns. i'll attach the logs retention options in the follow-up.
[03:35] Aisha Khan: can you also confirm SSO + SAML provisioning for RBAC? our security team insists on SCIM provisioning too.
[03:43] Maya Chen: yes, SSO SAML is supported; SCIM-based provisioning for users & roles is available on Enterprise plans. we'll include an integration checklist for SSO/SCIM.
[03:52] Jordan Lee: quick follow up on pricing — any ballpark for a dedicated pool sized for 1500 rps peak with 200 concurrent generation streams?
[04:01] Maya Chen: i'll be conservative here — i'll surface two options: dedicated reserved cluster sized for that throughput and a second larger cluster with burst capacity. i'll include estimated monthly cost and the committed discount bands.
[04:12] Priya Sharma: also, do you have recommendations on quantization to reduce cost? we've seen some quality lift in q8 but cost savings in q4.
[04:20] Owen Patel: yeah, Redwood Optimize can run a quick evaluation — we look at token distributions and latency vs. quality tradeoffs and recommend a quantization profile. we can generate a short report showing expected per-token cost reduction.
[04:30] Jordan Lee: awesome. any timing concerns to note for EU deployment? how long to provision Dedicated in eu with committed capacity?
[04:37] Owen Patel: provisioning usually takes 2-4 weeks depending on the exact GPU type and cloud region. if you want a guaranteed start date before holiday season, we should lock in the commitment in the next 10 business days to ensure capacity.
[04:48] Aisha Khan: procurement will need master service terms and an order form. will you be able to provide redlined terms?
[04:54] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send the standard MSA and an order form for the renewal. if Atlas needs changes to certain clauses, our legal ops will accept markups and we'll triage. i'll include the fall-back language for data residency and the KMS clause Samir mentioned.
[05:06] Carlos Mendes: last question from infra — during the benchmark, can we run with our traffic replay dataset? that would give realistic numbers.
[05:12] Owen Patel: absolutely, that's ideal. please share a sanitized replay or synthetic phantoms and we'll run the benchmark in the EU pool. we'll need a short spec: model version, prompt lengths, and expected concurrency.
[05:23] Jordan Lee: perfect. sounds like we're aligned. recap please?
[05:27] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Maya to send updated pricing for 12 vs 18 month with Dedicated and EU add-on, include SLA table and discount bands — due 2026-09-17. 2) Owen to run EU capacity benchmark with Atlas test dataset and share results — target to run next week, deliver by 2026-09-22. 3) Samir to share SOC2, SSO/SCIM checklist, and KMS/HSM integration notes — due 2026-09-18. 4) Atlas to confirm desired contract length and any redlines; procurement (Aisha) will coordinate with Maya.
[05:47] Aisha Khan: thanks, that's great. we'll aim to review pricing and come back with decision by 2026-09-24.
[05:55] Maya Chen: awesome. thanks all — i'll follow up with the docs and pricing after this call.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

References to shared artifacts: "Renewal pricing deck (link)", "EU benchmark plan (link)", "SOC2 report (link)" — links to be shared in follow-up email.
